value.reason: Line 21 of lib/insecurity.ts is masked as hard-coded signing material. On line 54, authorize() passes that privateKey straight to jwt.sign with RS256. This matches the positive example, where a literal signing key is defined in source and used to sign tokens. It does not match the negative example, which reads the key from process.env. Anyone who can read the source or the deployed bundle gets the private key and can forge valid JWTs for any user. That breaks authentication and access control, so the key does not stay confidential as a credential needs to (CWE-798). It also falls short of the reasonable access-control safeguards required for personal data the application handles.
